headline: Ward 37 trails 48 wards overall, though its ozone reading is the second lowest citywide.
summary:
Second from the bottom of Chicago's 50 wards, Ward 37 takes in Austin, Humboldt Park, Belmont Cragin, and West Garfield Park on the West Side. Its combined score lands it 49th of 50 citywide. That low number splits into two different pictures. A handful of measures here beat almost every other ward, while most of the rest land dead last.

The strongest results are how quickly the city closes graffiti requests, the ward's ozone reading, and the share of its infrastructure budget spent on sidewalk repair, each placing in the top five citywide. The weakest results all land in last place, and there are six of them. They cover diversity of religious traditions among local houses of worship, a modeled measure of social cohesion, school proficiency, a modeled estimate of how many adults work with neighbors on something for the community, licensed bars and taverns, and bank branches per resident.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers need a caveat attached. Fifth place on the wastewater-proximity score, which tracks pollution concentrated near local streams, is less impressive than it sounds. Thirty-five of the fifty wards crowd inside two points of the top score here, so fifth place mostly reflects a packed field. Bank branches per resident rank dead last, and that count comes from ZIP code areas that don't line up with ward borders, so the figure itself is labeled low confidence in the source data, and most wards sit within four points of one another on this measure anyway. Social cohesion also ranks last, but the number behind it is not a ward-specific count. It comes from a modeled ZIP code proxy, flagged low confidence the same way.

news.headline: City Rolls Out Stormwater Storage System On West Side After Near-Record Rainfall Strains Reservoirs
news.note: The city switched on a new underground stormwater storage pilot built to protect close to 3,000 homes across the 28th, 29th, and 37th wards after a weekend of near-record rainfall pushed the region's reservoirs close to capacity.

news.headline: Austin's Frank Lloyd Wright House, Among City's Most Endangered Buildings, Bought By Nonprofit
news.note: Austin Coming Together bought the J.J. Walser House, the West Side's only Frank Lloyd Wright-designed single-family home, and plans a multimillion-dollar restoration after years of disrepair.
